title: How Much Do We Really Want to Know About UFOs?
author: Kristen French
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPsychologyHow Much Do We Really Want to Know About UFOs?What disaster psychology research, a few Cold War UFO files, and a Spielberg movie say about how we might handle first contactKFBy Kristen French11:00 AM CDT on August 6, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleWhat would happen if the whole world, 7 billion people, learned all at once that they are not alone in the universe?That’s the premise of Steven Spielberg’s recent movie Disclosure Day. Two factions with different answers to this question battle it out across multiple chase scenes in cars, trains, and buses that stretch across the United States. (The movie’s theatrical run is almost over, but there are very few spoilers below.) On the one hand, a private intelligence firm called Wardex, in league with world governments, assumes that such a disclosure would cause worldwide panic and lead to total societal collapse. On the other, a group of former employees of Wardex, led by a man named Hugo, believe that the power of empathy and instinct for emotional connection would allow humans to handle it gracefully. Raising the stakes, Hugo and his defectors believe that a revelation of such cosmic proportions could shrink global conflict to a footnote and forestall impending World War III.Spielberg’s film debuted just as transparency about alien life became a hot topic on Capitol Hill. In May, the U.S. government began publicly releasing 80 years of classified files related to extraterrestrials, UAPs (unidentified anomalous phenomena), and UFOs (unidentified flying objects), including Cold War-era reports of rotating saucers, recent sightings of metallic elliptical objects hovering in military airspace, an archival Apollo 17 photo with three unexplained lights enlarged above the lunar terrain, and a one-hour, multi-witness UAP encounter observed from a military helicopter in late 2025. Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 OTD In Space - April 4: Last Un-crewed Apollo Test FlightShareNextStaySome of the videos and photos seem genuinely puzzling, but most experts say they have down-to-earth explanations: sensor anomalies, optical diffraction, highly advanced drones, unmarked research balloons, and space debris. So far, none of the files has provided any actionable scientific data or offered any conclusive evidence of alien life or non-human technology.Read more: “Why Haven’t We Heard from Extraterrestrials Yet?”Of course, it’s possible something revealing is still hiding in government files, which will be released in batches as they’re identified, or that something new will come to light. And anyway, alien life has always been popular fodder for conspiracy theories. Whatever is out there, some people think authorities need a plan for how to communicate it to the public to protect against the potential psychological shocks of UAP disclosure. In June, a Capitol Hill event called the Disclosure Forum brought together sitting members of Congress, scientists from institutions such as Harvard and Yale universities, whistleblowers, and former national security officials in the same room where the 1973 Watergate hearings took place to discuss the matter of disclosures about potential aliens and UAPs. Organizers cited polling showing roughly 89 percent of Republicans and 88 percent of Democrats want more government disclosure on UAP.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
